chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When a son of the al-mula'ana (cursing) mother dies, and he has brothers, his wealth is distributed according to the shares of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.ابْنُ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: Son of the mother who underwent al-mula'ana (mutual cursing procedure)
key_terms.سِهَامِ اللَّهِ: Shares of Allah (Quranic prescribed portions of inheritance)

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a son from the 'cursed mother' (Zawjat al-Mula'ana) distributed if he dies with brothers?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the son of al-mula'ana, despite his father's uncertainty due to the mutual cursing procedure, is treated as a full heir. The distribution of his estate among his brothers follows the standard Quranic shares (siham), affirming his legal status within the paternal lineage. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the son of al-mula'ana inherits from his father and is inherited by his relatives, distinguishing him from those with more ambiguous lineage statuses.
